chapter: Hopkins, the South and Stuff Smith
title: Taking over Stuff's band, then forming his own in Philadelphia and Washington
summary: After Moline he held the band together to New York until the bookings fell apart, then in 1942 organised his own group, playing the Bengazi in Washington and Philadelphia.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay, fine. (Laughs.) So you stayed out in California with Stuff for a year or more, and we're now in about the early forties.
Yeah, forty, forty --
And what happened after -- and yet you -- after the Moline incident with Stuff you never saw him again?
I'm trying to think. And when he came out of the hospital, no. No, no, I think I called, I talked
to him on the phone a couple of times, but I don't remember seeing him since then.
Well what happened to the band?
Stuff?
Well, the --
Well yeah, well he --
They took Stuff away, and the band was there, and you --
-- well he was --
Were you left with the band?
I took over. I took over, until we got back to New York, and we broke up because Joe Glaser had been booking it, and the bookings, you know.
Well it was booked as Stuff Smith. And without Stuff Smith it --
Yeah, I mean -- anyway, we got back together. I got the guys back together in New York, and safely, and whatnot, and that was it.
Did you -- were you back with Fats again after that? Or no more?
See, Fats died in '43, didn't he?
Yeah. Yeah. And I carried my same group -- I organized my same -- my group.
You organized --
After that, went to Philadelphia.
After Stuff?
Yeah.
Yeah, uh-huh.
And kept things going, and we worked Washington, D. C., the Ben-gazi, Philadelphia. Where else did I go?
